newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee rebounds from lows to extend gains.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee rebounds from lows to extend gains.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures erased early losses in afternoon trade on persistent fund shortcovering but scale-up origin sales knocked prices from their peaks.
"We are seeing continued fund buying, it has been quite aggressive and volume again is good," said one trader.
"There is a scale-up origin selling but there's no great tonnage at the moment," the trader said.
"The market made new highs which is technically good and continues to move ahead," he said. Traders traced little or no roaster interest as the market made its way higher.
By the finish, most-active March stood $12 firmer at $1,315 a tonne after falling to a session low of $1,280. It then rebounded to the day's high of $1,335, breaching chart resistance at $1,331.
Traders pegged the next major hurdle at $1,340-$1,350 area while support is seen at $1,270.
Today's advance followed Wednesday's steep gains which saw the benchmark March contract rising by a hefty $80 on the day.
Volume was again active at 12,170 lots, but down slightly from Wednesday's 16,700 -- the highest in months.
Options interest also picked up dramatically this week as a volatile futures market forced operators to take price insurance.
The main interest on Thursday focused on the March $1,200/$1,350 put spread.
On Wednesday, buy-stops at above $1,280 led investment funds to close positions after what some viewed as a recent bullish Brazilian crop report.
In overnight news, the Brazilian government coffee auction of 120,100 bags of stocks was completely sold out, implying that the domestic market was exceptionally tight.
"While local roasters are calling for an increase in the size of the auctions, for the moment it is merely bullish," GNI said in a commentary.
"It could also imply that there is little coffee available for export at present," it added.
Elswhere, El Salvador said its 1996/97 coffee crop is still seen ending five percent down over last cycle at 3.06 million 46-kg bags. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
